title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes, runbook patterns, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game-day guidance, and customer communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product stakeholders who participate in incident detection, mitigation, and follow-up.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production-facing services: API gateway, serving runtime, dedicated pools, private deployments control plane, telemetry and billing services.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; rather, it sets the company-wide process and templates.

Incident severity definitions and SLOs
------------------------------------
We use a 4-level severity model. Each severity includes target response and escalation windows. SLOs and threshold actions are included to align runbooks with business impact.

1) Sev 1 — Production outage, customer-impacting, broad (e.g., API 5xx across regions, control-plane down):
   - Customer impact: wide; many customers unable to use the platform.
   - Initial on-call response: 5 minutes.
   - Escalation: PagerDuty urgent escalation after 5 minutes.
   - Target mitigation window: 30 minutes (partial mitigation) / 4 hours (full recovery) depending on root cause.

2) Sev 2 — Major degradation (e.g., high latency beyond SLA for >10% of requests, degraded model quality for hosted API):
   - Initial on-call response: 15 minutes.
   - Escalation: Phone/SMS escalation after 15 minutes if not acknowledged.
   - Target mitigation window: 1 hour.

3) Sev 3 — Limited impact (single customer, single region, or background job failures):
   - Initial on-call response: 1 hour.
   - Target mitigation window: 24 hours or next business day depending on impact.

4) Sev 4 — Informational/maintenance events (non-customer impacting):
   - Handled by the service owner during business hours or via scheduled runbooks.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Primary on-call (Service Owner): first responder, owns triage, remediation actions, and incident timeline entries.
- Secondary on-call/backup: supports primary and takes over if primary unavailable.
- Incident Commander (IC): appointed for Sev 1/2 incidents when coordination across teams is required. IC handles stakeholder communications and post-incident review coordination.
- Scribe/Communications owner: records timeline, drafts status page/customer messages, and publishes initial incident communication.
- Engineering manager / Product lead: coordinates customer outreach for affected enterprise customers and prioritizes follow-up work.

On-call rotations and handoffs
-----------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week for primary on-call engineers, with secondary overlap where possible.
- Roster maintenance: PagerDuty roster managed by Eng SRE team; changes must be requested via the on-call-rotations Slack channel and recorded in the rotation spreadsheet.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed at shift start):
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and confirm notifications are working.
  2. Verify runbook access (Confluence links, runbook shortcuts).
  3. Review outstanding incidents assigned to you and open action items.
  4. Confirm contact methods (phone, Slack, backup).
  5. Announce yourself in #oncall-status Slack channel.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts: PagerDuty rules, automated alerts from Prometheus/Grafana, Sentry, Logs, or external monitoring (Datadog).
   - First action: acknowledge alert, open incident in the incident tracker (Confluence incident page template or the internal incident tracker), and record initial observations.

2) Triage
   - Determine scope and affected customers/regions.
   - Classify severity using definitions above.
   - Assign primary, secondary, scribe, and IC (if required).

3) Mitigation
   - Execute service-specific runbook steps (see Runbooks section).
   - If runbook does not resolve issue, collect evidence (logs, stack traces, metrics, recent deploys) and escalate to appropriate teams (infra, runtime, model-onboarding).

4) Recovery & Verification
   - Validate recovery with synthetic checks and customer verification where appropriate.
   - Monitor for recurrence for at least 2x the mean time to failure window.

5) Communications
   - Publish initial incident message to the status page within 15 minutes for Sev 1/2 and 60 minutes for Sev 3.
   - Provide regular updates every 30 minutes for Sev 1, every hour for Sev 2 until resolved.
   - Coordinate private customer notifications for affected enterprise accounts via customer-success.

6) Post-incident & Postmortem
   - Create a postmortem document (using the template below) within 72 hours of incident resolution.
   - Assign action items with owners and due dates.
   - Postmortem must be reviewed in the next SRE/Platform retro.

Runbooks (pattern + examples)
----------------------------
Runbook pattern (each runbook must include):
- Title / Service name
- Detection triggers (alerts/metrics)
- Triage checks (quick diagnostics)
- Immediate mitigation steps (1st, 2nd, 3rd order)
- Verification steps
- Rollback or mitigation play (if deploy related)
- Owner and escalation contacts
- Post-incident follow-up checklist

Example runbook: API 5xx spike
- Detection: 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 5 minutes across 3+ zones or 5xx rate > 0.5% for a tier-1 customer.
- Quick triage:
  1. Check gateway error logs (gateway-logs) and look for recent deploy IDs.
  2. Confirm upstream model-serving health (serving-runtime /metrics: request_success_ratio).
  3. Verify rate-limiter and auth-layer (quota service) are operating.
- Immediate mitigations:
  1. If deploy suspected: trigger canary rollback (use orchestrator UI / kubectl rollout undo).
  2. If overload: enable rate limiting or increase concurrency on dedicated pool for affected customers.
  3. If model-serving error: switch route to fallback model variant (per smart routing policy).
- Verification: synthetic request success > 99% for 10 minutes; customers report restored.
- Owner: API gateway on-call; Escalate to runtime leads if not resolved in 30 minutes.

Example runbook: GPU OOM / Node failure in Dedicated pool
- Detection: node OOM alerts from node-exporter, pod OOMKilled events, or scheduler backpressure.
- Triage:
  1. Identify affected pool and recent GPU utilization trends.
  2. Check autoscaler and queued-job metrics.
- Immediate mitigations:
  1. Drain affected node and migrate priority workloads.
  2. Scale up additional capacity if autoscaler not responding.
  3. Apply temp config to reduce batch sizes or concurrency for long-running jobs.
- Verification: job success rate returns to baseline and no OOM events for 15 minutes.

Game days and continuous readiness
--------------------------------
- Frequency: quarterly game days (minimum) with at least one cross-team scenario per cycle.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, on-call handoffs, cross-team coordination, and customer comms.
- Example scenarios: region outage, model-quality regression at scale, dedicated-pool capacity exhaustion.
- After action: game-day report with findings, owners for fixes, and timeline of events.

Status page & customer communications templates
---------------------------------------------
Public status guidance:
- For Sev 1/2 incidents, publish a public status page incident within 15 minutes. Include: title, impact statement, affected regions/services, current status, next update ETA.
- Template (public status page):
  - Title: [Service] — Partial outage impacting API requests
  - Impact: We are currently seeing elevated 5xx errors for requests to the hosted API in us-west-2. A subset of customers may experience failures or degraded performance.
  - Next update: 30 minutes
  - Contact: support@redwood-inference.com (for enterprise customers please contact your CSM)

Private customer communication (email/Slack) template (for enterprise customers):
- Subject: Incident [INC-YYYYMMDD-###] — Impact to Redwood API in us-west-2
- Hi <Customer Name>,

We are investigating elevated error rates affecting requests to the Redwood hosted API in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively triaging and mitigating.

Current impact: Some requests may fail with 5xx errors; latency may be elevated.
What we are doing: We have rolled back a recent deploy and routed traffic to a fallback model pool while we investigate root cause.
Estimated next update: 30 minutes

We will follow up with a full post-incident summary. If you need priority coordination, please reply to this message or contact your CSM.

Postmortem & RCA process
-------------------------
Postmortem structure (must be filled within 72 hours):
- Title and incident ID
- Severity and impact summary (customers, regions, duration)
- Timeline (timestamped events)
- Root cause analysis (why)
- Contributing factors
- Mitigations taken during the incident
- Long-term remediation and action items (owner + due date)
- Detection improvements and monitoring changes
- Lessons learned and communication notes

Action item governance:
- Action items must have a clear owner, target due date, and acceptance criteria.
- Engineering manager reviews overdue items in weekly team leads sync.

Incident metrics and dashboards
------------------------------
Key metrics to monitor and include in postmortems:
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) — target: < 5 minutes for Sev 1.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) — target: < 30 minutes for Sev 1 partial mitigation.
- Mean time to resolution (MTTR).
- Customer impact time (total minutes of customer-visible degradation).
- Error budget consumption per SLO.

Tooling and integrations
-----------------------
- PagerDuty: primary alerting and escalation.
- Slack (#oncall-status, #incident-ops): incident chatter, announcements, and handoffs.
- Confluence: incident page templates and postmortems.
- Statuspage (public): service status and public communications.
- Grafana/Prometheus, Sentry, ELK/Logsearch: telemetry sources.

Escalation matrix (quick reference)
----------------------------------
- On-call engineer -> Secondary -> Team lead -> Eng SRE -> Platform / Runtime lead -> CTO (for Sev 1 lasting > 4 hours or affecting > 20% customers).

Templates (copy-paste friendly)
------------------------------
1) Incident page template header:
   Title: [INC-YYYYMMDD-###] — <Short description>
   Severity: Sev 1 | Sev 2 | Sev 3 | Sev 4
   Primary on-call: <name>
   Secondary/backup: <name>
   Incident commander: <name>
   Scribe: <name>

2) Initial status page message (public):
   We are investigating elevated error rates affecting <service> in <region>. Some customers may experience failures or degraded performance. We will update by <ETA>.

3) Postmortem checklist:
   - [ ] Create postmortem in Confluence within 72 hours
   - [ ] Assign action items with owners and due dates
   - [ ] Schedule postmortem review meeting
   - [ ] Share postmortem with stakeholders and label as internal

Governance and training
-----------------------
- New on-call engineers must complete the on-call onboarding checklist and shadow two rotations before primary responsibility.
- Quarterly review of runbooks: each service must validate and sign off on their runbooks during the quarterly runbook sweep.
- Game days feed improvements into runbooks and monitoring; owners must close game-day action items within one sprint.

Related documents
-----------------
- SLO and error budget policies: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Incident communications & status page templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-communications-and-status-page-templates-2026
- Service-specific runbooks: see each service folder under /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks

Appendix: quick command snippets
-------------------------------
- Rollback a Kubernetes deployment:
  kubectl -n production rollout undo deployment/<service> --to-revision=<rev>
- Check gateway logs (example):
  kubectl -n gateway logs deploy/gateway --tail=200 | jq -C '.level, .message'
- Verify synthetic: curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.com/health | jq
